Currently, Vishal is involved in research projects focused on the Kosi River Basin in Bihar, India, and the MassDOT SSL project focused on train line safety and resilience in coastal Massachusetts. His ongoing research explores the removal of the embankments on the Kosi River, flood forecasting, and the assessment of vulnerability and adaptation strategies in the context of present and future climatic conditions, employing theoretical frameworks like Integrated Water Resource Management, System Dynamics modeling, and cost-benefit analysis under the supervision of Prof. Paul Kirshen from the School for the Environment (SFE). Vishal is passionate about synthesizing socio-hydro geomorphological dynamics, contributing to impactful research on climate change, policy formulation, and ecological crisis mitigation. 2. Currently, Vishal is involved in research projects focused on the Kosi River Basin in Bihar, India, and the MassDOT SSL project focused on train line safety and resilience in coastal Massachusetts. His ongoing research explores the removal of the embankments on the Kosi River, flood forecasting, and the assessment of vulnerability and adaptation strategies in the context of present and future climatic conditions, employing theoretical frameworks like Integrated Water Resource Management, System Dynamics modeling, and cost-benefit analysis under the supervision of Prof. Paul Kirshen from the School for the Environment (SFE). Vishal is passionate about synthesizing socio-hydro geomorphological dynamics, contributing to impactful research on climate change, policy formulation, and ecological crisis mitigation.
